title: paged-kv-cache-block-manager-reuse-pinning-optimizations
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Reduce allocation churn, lock contention, and premature eviction in the paged KV cache block manager. This PR introduces block reuse and a lightweight pinning mechanism to keep actively referenced blocks from being evicted during GC or compaction. It also reduces global allocator contention by introducing per-shard freelists and a fast-path for common allocation sizes. The result is lower CPU overhead, reduced memory fragmentation on GPU, and fewer stalls during continuous batching under high concurrency.

Scope: Changes are limited to the paged KV cache layer and improve allocator behavior and block lifecycle. No API changes to serving or customers. Includes unit and integration tests plus a small benchmark harness.

Summary of changes (high level): implemented reuse path in BlockAllocator; added Block::pin/unpin semantics and pin-count tracking; introduced per-shard freelists with a fallback global pool; updated eviction heuristics to respect pinned blocks and a configurable pin TTL; reduced allocator lock hold time and replaced some coarse locks with atomic ops; added metrics for allocation/sec, reuse-rate, pin-count, and eviction-skipped; added bench and regression tests.

Compatibility/Rollout: Feature gated behind runtime flag "kv.paged.block_reuse=true" and pinning defaulted on. Can be reverted by disabling the flag at runtime or rolling back the config. Carefully tested with Dedicated and Hosted load profiles.

Benchmarks: Under synthetic continuous-batching load (1k concurrent requests, seq len 1024) observed: 12-18% reduction in CPU p95 for the serving worker threads, 9% lower GPU memory fragmentation (measured via allocator high-water patterns), and 22% reduction in allocator lock contention on heavy-multi-request traces. Bench harness and raw data attached in benches/ directory.

Testing: unit tests for allocator reuse paths, pin/unpin race conditions, and GC interactions. Integration test exercising eviction under high concurrency and functional tests for correctness of KV lookup post-eviction.

Notes: This PR focuses on allocator-level and block-manager improvements. Future work: adaptive pin TTL, smarter eviction based on usage heatmap, and exposing reuse metrics to the Console for operator diagnostics.

review_comments: Jordan Li: Can you clarify how pinning interacts with the existing TTL-based eviction? We need to ensure long-lived pins don't cause unbounded memory growth.

Ava Martinez (author): Pins now carry a TTL and count toward a pinned-memory metric; eviction will skip pinned blocks until pin TTL expires. The TTL default is conservative (30s) and is configurable per-deployment.
Priya Anand: The per-shard freelist looks good. Please add a unit test that forces cross-shard allocations to ensure fallback global pool works.
Ava Martinez: Added tests that intentionally create cross-shard allocation pressure and verify correctness; updated description and tests list.
Marcus Green: Observed a flaky failure in bench CI where reuse-rate drops to zero under low-load; are we disabling reuse for tiny allocations anywhere?
Ava Martinez: Good catch — discovered a bug in the small-block fast-path. Pushed fix in commit g7c0d1e and re-ran benchmarks. CI benches passed on rerun.
Jordan Li: Approving after verifying the metrics and bench results locally. Major risk areas documented.
release_notes: Improved paged KV cache block allocator with block reuse, pinning to prevent eviction of active blocks, lower lock contention, and new metrics. Rollout behind kv.paged.block_reuse flag. Expected lower CPU p95 and reduced fragmentation under continuous batching workloads.
notes: Metrics added: kv_allocator_allocs, kv_allocator_reuses, kv_pin_count, kv_eviction_skipped
